name: Palmetto Bay Village Council

meetings.pattern: Regular council meeting once a month, usually the first Monday, 7:00 p.m., Village Hall Council Chambers, 9705 East Hibiscus Street, Palmetto Bay, FL 33157; hybrid (in person and online). Zoning hearings on a later Monday at 7:00 p.m. Charter Sec. 4.1(A) requires at least 11 regular monthly meetings a year.

schedule.note: Regular Council Meeting, Village Hall Council Chambers; schedule is marked preliminary and the council may change it by vote
Regular Council Meeting, Village Hall Council Chambers
Zoning and Land Development Permit Hearing

phases.name: Budget workshops and mid-year town halls with the Village Manager
phases.decides: Council and residents review the manager's spending plan before the proposed millage is set; the 2026 workshops were June 23 and July 28 (schedule page) with a Budget Workshop on July 20 on the agenda portal.

phases.name: First budget hearing (tentative millage and budget)
phases.decides: Tentative millage rate and tentative FY 2026-27 budget, 7:00 p.m., held with the September regular council meeting.

phases.name: Second budget hearing (final millage and budget)
phases.decides: Final millage rate and the FY 2026-27 budget ordinance, 7:00 p.m. Charter Sec. 4.5(B) requires adoption on or before September 30.

phases.name: Fiscal year begins
phases.decides: Charter Sec. 4.6: fiscal year runs October 1 through September 30.

phases.name: Candidate qualifying for the November 3, 2026 election
phases.decides: Who is on the ballot for Mayor, Council Seat 1 and Council Seat 3; noon August 3 to noon August 14, 2026, filed with the Village Clerk.

phases.name: Village general and special election
phases.decides: Mayor, Council Seat 1, Council Seat 3, and six charter amendment questions; polls 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

phases.name: Runoff, if needed
phases.decides: Runoff for any 2026 race without a majority winner, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

levers.how: Speak in person at Village Hall or live online by registering through the GoToWebinar link in each meeting's public notice; phone-only attendees cannot speak. Comments on agenda items can also be left through the e-comment feature on the agenda tab of the village site.
levers.rules: No time limit stated in the meeting notice or on the schedule page. Speakers address the mayor and follow decorum rules in Village Code Sec. 2-45. Comment forms are not accepted for quasi-judicial items. Charter Sec. 4.1(D): meetings end at midnight unless extended.
levers.deadline: Register for live online comment before the meeting through the notice's GoToWebinar link

levers.how: Submit the online Public Comments Form. Forms received before 5 p.m. on the day of the council meeting are read aloud by the Village Clerk for one minute during the meeting; later submissions go into the record but are not read.
levers.rules: Comments that attack or insult another person, or contain explicit or foul language, are placed in the record but not read aloud. Not available for quasi-judicial items.
levers.deadline: 5 p.m. on the day of the meeting to be read aloud

levers.how: Email or call the mayor and council members directly from the village directory; main line 305-259-1234.
levers.rules: Village Hall hours Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

levers.how: File a public records request through the village's JustFOIA portal; the Village Clerk is the records custodian.

Citizen initiative: at least ten electors file an affidavit to start; the petition needs signatures of at least 5 percent of electors registered at the last regular village election, filed within 60 calendar days. The clerk certifies within 20 days; if the council does not adopt the ordinance within 45 days it goes to a vote 30 to 60 days later. Initiatives cannot cover the budget, capital program, appropriations, taxes or salaries.
levers.rules: Charter Sec. 5.2(A)(1), (B), (C)(1), (C)(4), (D)(1), (E)(1), (E)(2), (F)(1). Charter amendments by petition follow Sec. 6.03 of the Miami-Dade Home Rule Charter (Charter Sec. 6.1(A)).
levers.deadline: 60 calendar days from the affidavit to file signatures

levers.how: Electors may require the council to reconsider any adopted ordinance (same exclusions as initiative). Same 5 percent signature threshold and 60-day filing window; the clerk certifies within five business days; if the council does not repeal within 30 days the ordinance goes to the voters and is repealed if a majority votes for repeal.
levers.deadline: 60 calendar days from the affidavit to file signatures

levers.how: Electors may recall the mayor or a council member as permitted by Florida law. The charter sets the signatures needed to start at 10 percent of electors registered at the last regular village election; the rest of the procedure (30-day collection window, defense statement, second-round petition of 15 percent) follows Fla. Stat. 100.361.
levers.deadline: 30 days for the first round of signatures under state law

levers.how: File a written notice of candidacy with the Village Clerk during the qualifying window and pay the $100 village qualifying fee plus the state election assessment (1 percent of salary: $240 mayor, $120 council). Two years of continuous village residency required.
levers.rules: Charter Sec. 2.4; 2026 window was noon August 3 to noon August 14. Term limits: Charter Sec. 2.3(E), two consecutive terms in one office, three combined.
levers.deadline: Noon on the last day of the qualifying period

levers.how: Vote in the November 3, 2026 general and special election (Mayor, Seats 1 and 3, six charter questions); runoff December 1, 2026 if needed. Early voting schedule is posted by the county.
levers.rules: Registered voters living in the village.
levers.deadline: Election day November 3, 2026, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

levers.how: Village boards and committees (Parks and Recreation, Art in Public Places, Resiliency, Tree Advisory, Education Advisory, Youth Community Involvement Task Force, Veterans' Park Task Force) meet monthly at Village Hall or Coral Reef Park; the 2026 Charter Revision Commission met January through June.

elections.terms: Four years, at large, staggered. General election in each even year on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November (Charter Sec. 5.1(C)). 2026: Mayor, Council Seat 1, Council Seat 3. 2028: Vice Mayor and Council Seat 2. Two consecutive terms per office, three combined (Sec. 2.3(E)). A 2026 ballot question proposes single-member districts and changed term limits.

notes: Checked 2026-10-22. Agenda lead days unknown: the Granicus video portal blocks automated fetching and the Meeting Central page does not state a posting rule; the agenda PDFs are on the granicusideas.com e-comment site. Budget hearing dates (Sep 14 and Sep 23, 2026) come from the agenda portal's past-meeting list, not a legal ad; the proposed budget release date was not found. Public comment time limit for in-person speakers not stated in the notice; only the one-minute reading of written forms is published. Village Code Sec. 2-45 (decorum) was not read because municode.com returned errors. Charter text is from the village's own PDF (DocumentCenter 2020), amended through 2016; the 2020 and 2026 charter amendments are not reflected in it. The 2026 election page's qualifying notice PDFs carry a 2024 label; dates used here are from the page body and the Qualifying as a Candidate page.
